content.value_statement: Existing Convex applications can accumulate security, scaling, dependency, and observability gaps. This skill creates a prioritized plan and applies approved improvements.
actual_capabilities: Detects a Convex application, its schema, and its deployment type.
Uses launch-readiness to obtain a scored, deduplicated assessment.
Checks pinned Convex components for stale versions.
Offers Sentinel installation when production error capture is missing.
Combines findings into a prioritized remediation plan.
Applies confirmed fixes and reports the readiness score change.
limitations: Requires an existing Convex application with a detectable convex directory.
Depends on launch-readiness, check-updates, and Sentinel capabilities when those actions are needed.
Does not apply changes without explicit user confirmation.
Does not replace independent production testing or operational review.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Convex Release
use_cases.description: Assess launch readiness, prioritize security issues, and verify improvements before a production release.

use_cases.title: Review Platform Health
use_cases.description: Combine readiness, component freshness, and observability findings into one ordered remediation plan.

use_cases.title: Modernize an Existing App
use_cases.description: Identify stale Convex components and missing error capture before approving targeted updates.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Basic Assessment
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this Convex application and present its readiness score with the highest-priority fixes. Do not change files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when beginning a review of an existing application.

prompt_templates.title: Check Components and Monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess this application, check pinned Convex components for updates, and identify any production observability gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when reviewing dependencies and error monitoring.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Confirmed Fix Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a prioritized remediation plan for this Convex application. Explain each change, then wait for my confirmation before applying anything.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when preparing controlled remediation work.

prompt_templates.title: Optimize and Measure Results
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess the application, include upgrades and observability work, request approval, apply approved fixes, then report the new score and remaining risks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Use for an end-to-end optimization with measured results.

output_examples.input: Assess this Convex application without changing files.
output_examples.output: Readiness score: 78. Address authorization findings first, then update stale components and add production error capture.

output_examples.input: Apply the approved fixes and reassess the application.
output: Applied the confirmed authorization and component updates.
Production error capture remains pending approval.

best_practices: Begin with the read-only assessment before proposing changes.
Prioritize security and data-loss findings before maintenance improvements.
Review the score change and remaining risks after every approved update.
anti_patterns: Do not bypass confirmation before modifying an existing application.
Do not repeat delegated audit passes manually.
Do not prioritize style changes above security or data-loss risks.

faq.question: Does this skill modify my application immediately?
faq.answer: No. It starts with a read-only assessment and requires explicit confirmation before applying changes.

faq.question: What does the initial assessment include?
faq.answer: It uses launch-readiness to produce a scored, deduplicated report and an ordered fix plan.

faq.question: Can it identify outdated Convex components?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks pinned Convex components and adds stale-component findings to the remediation plan.

faq.question: How does it address observability?
faq.answer: It offers Sentinel installation when the readiness report identifies missing production error capture.

faq.question: How are fixes prioritized?
faq.answer: Security and data-loss risks come first, followed by upgrades, observability, and lower-priority improvements.

faq.question: How does it verify improvements?
faq.answer: After approved changes, it reruns the readiness assessment and reports the score difference.
